subject: general
question:
From the alternatives given below, select the correct meaning of the idiom.
The penny drops.

options.text: Said when someone suddenly comes to realize or understand something
Said when someone suddenly comes to feel angry about something
Said when someone suddenly comes to bends to pick something
Said when someone suddenly comes to feel loved by somebody

solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 1 i.e. "Said when someone suddenly comes to realize or understand something"**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"The penny drops"** means the moment when someone suddenly realizes or understands something clearly. (जब किसी को अचानक कुछ स्पष्ट रूप से समझ में आता है।)
 
 
 
• **Example:** It took me a while to understand the joke, but then the penny dropped, and I burst out laughing.
 
 
 
• This idiom is commonly used in situations where the realization comes after a delay or hesitation.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 1 i.e. "Said when someone suddenly comes to realize or understand something"**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Option 2:** **Said when someone suddenly comes to feel angry about something** (जब किसी को अचानक गुस्सा महसूस होता है।)
 
 
• **Example:** This option is incorrect because "The penny drops" does not relate to feelings of anger.
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** **Said when someone suddenly bends to pick something** (जब कोई अचानक कुछ उठाने के लिए झुकता है।)
 
 
• **Example:** This option is incorrect as "The penny drops" is not related to physical actions like bending down.
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** **Said when someone suddenly comes to feel loved by somebody** (जब कोई अचानक किसी द्वारा प्यार महसूस करता है।)
 
 
• **Example:** This option is incorrect as the idiom does not refer to feelings of love or affection.
